html:
Marcus Garvey was a Jamaican activist, born in St Ann's Bay in 1887, who founded the Universal Negro Improvement Association in 1914. It became the largest Black mass movement in history.

From New York in the 1920s he preached Black pride, self-reliance and a return to Africa. His shipping firm, the Black Star Line, failed, and he was convicted of mail fraud in the United States and deported to Jamaica in 1927. He died in London in 1940.

His ideas shaped Pan-Africanism and leaders such as Kwame Nkrumah, and the followers of Rastafari saw him as a prophet. Jamaica brought his body home in 1964 and named him its first National Hero.
sum: Marcus Garvey was a Jamaican activist, born in St Ann's Bay in 1887, who founded the Universal Negro Improvement Association in 1914. It became the largest Black mass movement in history.
